name: Boat
needs: Navigable water from landing to landing: the sea, bays, estuaries, rivers and lakes, and streams and marsh channels at least 8 m wide (a raft or canoe of the small-draft kind, poled or paddled). Open sea needs a sea-going operator at both ends.
operated_by: Raft-masters and canoe-men on the inland water; harbour boatmen and lighter-men in the ports, on small-draft coasters of Dunmer and Imperial build.
evidence: Skyrim's carriages and the Dragonborn boat: a driver or boatman's topic per destination, a fixed fare gated on the player's gold, Game.FastTravel to the destination's marker (Skyrim.esm DialogueCarriageSystem, CarriageCost 20, CarriageCostSmall 50; the Northern Maiden, 250 to Solstheim). Morrowind's shipmasters: a port-to-port ring along the coast with fares by distance ('I can transport you ... for a modest fee', morrowind-full.json).
why: Small-draft boats are 'the most common and the fastest form of transportation, both of people and goods, inside Argonia' (Lore:Sea Transportation); personal rafts are the default vehicle (The Argonian Account, Bk 4); the province's network 'exists, and most of it is water' (story/lore/extrapolation/argonia-4e201-state.md, Routes).

name: Coach
needs: A major road the whole way (road class major: the cart road); minor tracks and footpaths do not carry a cart.
operated_by: Carters with lizard-drawn carts on the old Imperial roads of the west and north.
evidence: Skyrim's carriages: a driver at the stable takes the fare and fast-travels the player (DialogueCarriageSystem); vanilla's flat 20 and 50 are replaced here by a fare by road length, as Morrowind's silt striders charge by distance.
why: Imperial roads survive in pieces: the Blackwood Road to Gideon, the stone roads of Stormhold, the roads of the Gideon plain (story/lore/extrapolation/argonia-4e201-state.md, Routes). Horses bog down in the marsh, so the Hist shaped lizards into the forms of horses; Bright-Throats breed horse-lizards (story/lore/topics/fauna-hazards.md).

name: Rootworm
needs: A Hist tree with a root pool at both ends: the rootworm runs through tunnels formed by the roots of the Hist trees and surfaces at a spire of bubbles from an underground stream.
operated_by: A root-tender at each Hist who calls the worm to the root pool and sees the traveller swallowed.
evidence: Skyrim's flat carriage fare (CarriageCost) for a route with no road to measure; Morrowind's Mages Guild guides and propylon chambers for a fixed link between a few named halls.
why: The Underground Express: rootworms swallow travellers whole and carry them at speed through tunnels formed by the roots of Hist trees; Gideon is a canon stop, marked by red clay (Lore:Rootworm; story/lore/regions/middle-argonia.md; story/lore/gideon.md). Helstrom is reached early by rootworm (story/lore/extrapolation/argonia-4e201-state.md).
